tool_args.prompt: Create ONE complete transparent-background character image of Colmillos from ORIGINAL Resident Evil 4 (2005), in the precise phase shown in the two attached references: the dark canine with the long thin dorsal Plaga appendages already deployed. Both references depict the SAME source render; the second is only a clearer light-background corroboration, not a second creature. Isolate that one complete canine and its connected appendages. Preserve the lean dark charcoal-brown coarse coat, source head with pointed ears and canine teeth, four anatomically coherent legs with complete paws, and the source's short raised bushy tail. Preserve the visible arrangement of long thin whip-like dorsal appendages and their looping curves and tapering ends; do not replace them with thick octopus tentacles or add extra branches, heads, jaws, wings, spines or limbs. Match the visible source rather than the 2023 remake or a new monster design. Show a clear SCREEN-RIGHT facing side-dominant three-quarter stance close to the documented source orientation, with the head, chest and forepaws aimed to the right. Do not invent an opposite-side reconstruction. Keep every paw, ear, tail tip and EVERY dorsal appendage tip inside the image, including the very high thin tip that is tightly framed in the low-resolution reference. Scale the WHOLE subject down to leave at least 10 percent clean transparent margin around its full silhouette; the tall appendages are part of the subject and must not be cropped. The reference can only support a static visual adaptation, so preserve its broad form without pretending to recover original mesh or texture detail. Clean real transparent alpha, one canine only, no floor, background, cast backdrop shadow, badge, watermark, border, text, logo, collage or animation grid. Omit the watermark and layout behind the source entirely. Preserve the source appearance without adding injuries or a violent scene. Do not horizontally mirror an image. This is a single newly generated static candidate for review, not an engine-ready animation or certified native asset.
